# Chapter Eleven: Maelen

Where am I Marcus wondered, his mind awash with death and fire as images of the cabin played through his mind, however, around him was silence save the simple calls of animals echoing around him, opening his eyes he found himself in the green and brown of the early winter’s woods.

I am back in the forest; I have come full circle he thought looking around. A fire stood in the middle of the small clearing, the flames playing over a spit as something hung on a spit, cooking, the sound of fat sizzling and falling into the flames causing him to wince as the memories of the cabin flashed in his mind. “ORAH” he shouted sitting up as pain radiated up his side threatening to send him back into blackness.

“Woah there, partner, you might want to take it slow, you have had a hell of time there hoss” came an old gravelly voice from behind him.

Marcus snapped his head around causing more pain to shoot up his neck and his eyes to water. As they began to clear he saw an old man, his downy white long hair and matching bearded framed tanned rough skin and grey wary eyes, a set of broad white teeth matching the beard, but the disarming and genuine smile also revealed kindness. He crouched over a pack leisurely digging through it as he talked

The old man was dressed in some kind of black leather outfit, one that reminded Marcus of a uniform with buckles crossing the chest, waist and along the arms holding it snugly in place, the brass buckles a contrast to the black leather of the outfit.

Marcus’s eyes were drawn to the green sash the man wore around his waist, the piece of color on the outfit.

The man looked as if he could handle himself, he looked limber and quick for his age, if this man attacked without weapons Marcus knew he would have a hell of a time beating him despite the age difference.

Who is this guy he wondered, Marcus had never seen this man before and tensed as the man slowly approached hands outstretched in a calming gesture?

“Who the fuck are you” Marcus shot at him putting as much menace into the words as possible. “The guy who saved your life and got you out of dodge hoss, otherwise you would probably be sitting in a cell for Barbequing the Lord Seer’s tax collectors. He tends to frown upon things like that, not to mention the Empress and a few other head honcho’s have a keen interest in finding you and doing who knows what, so I would be a little more thankful in your tone there hoss” he admonished him and then a stunning realization hit Marcus, the words, that accent he knew that accent, though light and not as pronounced as it probably was in the man’s younger days, it was unmistakable, Texas.

“Your speaking English, how the fuck are you speaking English?” he asked his eyes narrowing as he studied the man. The old man smiled “Call me Maelen and like you I came from the ARC ships, just about two decades before you did” he finished pointing at the sky and taking another tentative step towards him.

“Like you, I have the power, power that has not been seen in this world for centuries” he continued and slowly pushing his hand out to his side Marcus watched in amazement as a large branch levitated from the ground, hanging just below the man’s hand.

“Okay, so you’re from my earth, I got that part and you’re a mage” Marcus stated, his mind raced, trying to remember the events after the cabin, how had he gotten here he continued to search his memory for any detail that would reveal the answer.

Then his mind returned to the six burning men, the faces now seared into his soul as they burst into flames, he had taken the lives of six men in an instant. And then he remembered the bundle in his arms as he had stood there watching them die. “Where is Orah?” Marcus asked panicked, everything else forgotten as he searched the area around him and not finding any sign of the bundle or the woman.

Maelen slowly walked over and crouched by the fire, turning the spit to cook whatever was on it evenly. “I buried her, you have been here for a four days unconscious my friend, she did not make it and a lot has happened I need to fill you in on, we don’t have a lot of time” he finished his tone gentle but urgent.

Marcus knew she was dead, the memory of the body, the smoldering and burnt bundle he carried from the cabin, was seared into his soul. The woman he loved, a smoking charred body, a mass of smoldering meat carried gently in his arms from the scene of her death.

Canting his head back he unleashed a scream, one that hurt his very soul as his body began to shake from the effort he screamed for the death of the woman he would have gladly spent the rest of his life with and ultimately, he screamed because he was left alive, he would have gladly traded his life for hers.

Then the worst thought he had ever passed through his head. Would she still be alive if she had never met him, he wondered, and the weight of that question crushed what little soul he had left.

Marcus collapsed into tears curling up into a fetal position continuing to cry as his body spasmed from the weight of the grief. Maelen didn’t try to comfort him, didn’t try to talk, he just crouched there, waiting for him to work through what was possibly the worst thing to happen to this man.

Eventually Marcus stopped crying, he lay there staring at the trees not speaking as his mind tried to resolve the death of his life.

Maelen continued to remain quiet, taking a piece of the sizzling meat off of the fire and cutting it with a large knife from the leather sheath on his belt.

Laying the meat on a wooden plate in front of Marcus he paused for a moment “I’m sorry hoss” he said and the sadness In his voice was genuine.

Marcus simply stared ahead, unmoving and unresponsive, Maelen sighed standing and looking the other man over, with a shake of his head he walked away from the fire leaving Marcus to his grief.

The older man entered the dense underbrush as Marcus watched him disappear into the forest.

The rest of night He lay there, staring at the food, not wanting to eat, instead replaying in vivid detail finding Orah’s body and the events that followed. Eventually, mercifully he passed out from exhaustion his body shutting down and putting him in a deep dreamless sleep the pain and severity of his wounds overcoming his need to process the soul crushing grief.

He awoke the next morning with a start as bright light seared into his eyes, his head exploded with pain. “Maelen” Marcus croaked covering his eyes and trying to hold his skull together.

“Here hoss, try this” the gravelly voice said, and Marcus felt leaves being placed in his hand, at urging from the older man, he placed them in his mouth and began to chew, instantly his headache began to subside, and a calm fell over his mind, Maelen grinned at him “Xanax and Percocet never had an effect like that huh” he said grinning in triumph.

Marcus sat quietly for a moment allowing the herb to take full effect and then looked up at the older man “You said things have happened?” he asked and watched as Maelen’s face fell.

“Our meeting was no accident hoss, in fact since you first got here we have been watching you, luckily Lawrence in town knew what you were when you took the test and immediately contacted me” he began and Marcus stopped him “what test, I didn’t take any test” he said trying to recall his interaction with the shopkeeper in town. Maelen smiled “Someone would have handed you a small crystal, it measures your power” he said, and Marcus recalled the young man placing such a thing in his palm and then taking it back again.

Now a few of his interactions began to make sense, the old mage giving him the books made sense and he nodded. Maelen played with the fire for a moment, putting more wood on it before continuing.

“As I said, no accident, we have been keeping watch as events have unfolded, seen the lengths that the Empress and the other nation states have put into finding you hoss, they want you bad but we aren’t sure why, so we waited, doing our best to ensure you weren’t found and then the collectors happened, so I had to get you out of there, it wasn’t the way I wanted to introduce you to myself and the order, but it was either that or leave you to the Lord Seer” he continued looking to Marcus who said regarding the older man. “What is the Order?” he asked Maelen nodded expecting the question.

“The Order of the Dragon, we are the order of Mages created centuries ago to train, police and govern mages, even within that order however there are those who would see you captured and studied, those who are desperate to return to a time when we had great power and abilities, over the generations those powers have withered and some think that the end of the mage is in sight, they would use that to justify dissecting you to find out if your power could be taken, transferred or replicated” Maelen looked up to see the shocked look on Marcus’s face. “I know, the Order should be a sanctuary for you, but know this, it isn’t. There are those of us who believe differently.

When I arrived, a few within the order hid my origins and trained me, bringing me into the order and into the group, those of us who watch and wait for other fallen to arrive, to protect and train them” he said.

“I was assigned to find you and to train you, we need to prepare you to defend yourself Marcus, I fear you have enemies coming from every direction, the world as we know it is falling apart and death has come to the world” Maelen looked over towards the woods, Marcus could make out the worry and fear on his face.

“Why me Maelen, why do you care?” he asked, the older man sighed “If the Empress is doing what we suspect she is, then she is breaking the Agreement, which will mean War Marcus, the Mages will, for the first time in centuries have to fight for our lives and you and I represent hope to our people, the power we wield will make the difference if it comes to it” he answered, Marcus didn’t know what to say, so he simply said nothing.

“It’s a shitty position, but we need you” Maelen finished “Besides, you need to learn how to use what you have, or people could get hurt” he began but Marcus interrupted him “Dammit, people HAVE been hurt” he stated and then turned back to the fire, turning his back on Maelen and ending the conversation. He stared at the fire absently, if he was to be believed Maelen had come from the ARC, landed like Marcus and had lived and learned how to use the powers that he himself was just beginning to understand.

Hell, Maelen might know why they had landed so late and what happened to their earth, bottom line Maelen had answers, he could train him to control his powers, he didn’t care about the Mages or the country, the only thing he cared about was gone, with nothing left to him, the choice was easy he thought.

Marcus opened his mouth to answer him, but the words died in his throat, nothing as important anymore, nothing mattered, he just wanted Orah back.

Despite his mind’s calm, there was a pit, a deep black void that sat in the middle of his soul and Marcus never thought he would ever be able to mend it, he looked to this man, this fellow member of the project that put him here realizing in this world, this man was all Marcus had left.

Turning to Maelen he asked the one question he desperately wanted the answer to “What did they do to us?” Marcus almost whispered a tone of desperation in his voice like a man hanging onto the remnants of his sanity like a life raft as the shark’s circle.

Maelen regarded him for a moment and just when Marcus thought he wouldn’t say anything Maelen began to speak.

“When they prepared us for the ARC ships, they did something to us, changed us injecting something into our bodies I really don’t think they understood what it would do, or how it would change us, they didn’t do it out of malice but desperation I believe.

But whatever was done, changed us on a cellular level, effecting our DNA and allowing us to somehow connect with the crystals that we found everywhere when we landed, whatever they are, seem to be tied to what was done to us and possibly to what was done to the planet by that machine.” he surmised not looking at Marcus but instead staring transfixed at the hypnotic flames licking over the day old empty spit.

Marcus recalled with detached interested the tests and the treatments, the DNA therapy and the injections day after day.

Recalling the days and weeks spent preparing for the journey he couldn’t resolve the mundane medical with his ability to set people on fire, how was that even possible he wondered.

Somewhere in his now lapse, strict catholic upbringing came the whispered question. Was he a monster and the thing that scared him most was that couldn’t answer that?

“Maelen, tell me what happened to our world” Marcus pleaded meeting the other man’s steel grey eyes, his own now wet with the tears of renewed grief that even the herbs couldn’t keep at bay, his expression silently pleaded with the other man to explain this.

Maelen looked back at the fire, gathering his thoughts his face growing serious, all traces of the joviality now gone. Finally, he spoke never taking his eyes from the fire, but Marcus could see the sorrow in the man’s face as he recited what he knew.

“First you have to remember we only have some written accounts and none of them are complete, but the Order has been able to put together a basic idea of what happened. I mean we don’t even have an idea of timeframe so we could be talking a thousand generations or a hundred” he said finally turning to look at Marcus the frustration evident in his eyes.

Marcus nodded, recalling the calendar he had seen in the church. The year displayed as 176 AA the ‘AA’ standing for Aurtus’s ascension so even that was suspect he recalled thinking at the time. Marcus motioned for the older man to go on. Maelen nodded and with a deep sigh recalled what little had had been able to find out.

“We were racing against the clock, the machine was counting down but we didn’t have an accurate idea of what it would do or when so The project itself was fighting an uphill battle, they rushed, cut corners and did things that never would have been done in the name of saving humanity, aside from some glitches, thus the reason we both are sitting here, and not long dead, seemed to go as planned and the ARC ships lifted off, hung in space and then dropped twenty thousand of our fellow humans back to earth when it was supposed to.

But they were unprepared for what had happened on our planet. Once back they realized that nothing of our civilization was left, whatever that machine did, removed any trace of mankind from the planet, everything, leaving only the planet itself along with the animals and plants, but even those had been altered, almost as if someone had come along and factory reset the damn globe and unchecked the human option.” Maelen recalled shaking his head.

Marcus wasn’t quite sure how to take that. What he had said was impossible Marcus thought he just hadn’t traveled enough to see the monuments to his once great civilization, he truly expected to come across some derelict city, now large towers of crumbing ruins but if what Maelen said happened then they were gone.

The two men sat there silently as Marcus tried to digest the ramifications of what the older man had said, finally Maelen continued.

“The project had been created to save humans, giving a few emergency supplies and people with the knowledge to turn back on the power and bring up the computers but those were gone. The few supplies were quickly expended, the group went in search of the emergency bunkers that had been setup for us upon returning” he stated, and Marcus remembered the plan.

According to the ARC briefing there were emergency caches setup all over the country with everything you would need to bring civilization back. But if they had returned to earth and truly everything was gone. Then they would only have the few supplies the pods came with.

Maelen shifted, allowing him to turn and face Marcus “They quickly found out those caches were no longer there, the population had no support from the ARC project, they were on their own, and if that wasn’t enough, almost immediately they found the large growth formations of crystals growing everywhere.

Now we had a few geologists who were part of that group. According to their notes, these covered most of the surface and below, but they were not any formation that anyone could recognize, what little tests they were able to perform showed the crystal formations were made up of particles of metals, plastics and a lot of things that could have been found on our world back when humans were at the top of the food chain.

But there were also exotic elements they couldn’t identify.” He continued and Marcus glanced uncomfortably at a growth near the closest tree its ember coloring reflecting the sunlight making it through the skeletal canopy of the treetops. Was that all that was left as a testament to his civilization he wondered, if so, what the hell were they?

“After the first year, things started to break down and from what little we have in the ways of diaries and logs the survivors broke into factions, they began fighting over how best to build humanity back on the planet, who should lead and things like that.

Luckily a lot of them were military so feeding themselves and basic shelters were knowledge they had. But things like metal working, advanced construction, building hydro power plants were all beyond them and the tools they had.

Our whole civilization had returned to a hunter gatherer stage and began to form tribes, as food became scarce tribes raided others, some people lost their mind, not able to cope with what had happened and became cannibals. But after that first-year people began to notice that they could sense crystals, they could find them as if their brains could home in on them. Then someone figured out that they could draw energy from the crystals, and eventually discovered the ability to use that energy to power there will.

They spent years discovering the bounds of their abilities, the fighting settled down as they had other things to focus on, people began to live in peace and rediscovered farming, it was during these peaceful years when they began to truly experiment, one woman discovered the ability to create focal runes, using crystal dust and an odd quuniform language, we still don’t know its origin, she was able to alter weapons, clothing and other items that could not only focus the person’s will but with the right set of runes create spells that a person could power”.

Maelen held up his hand, turning over the black leather glove, Marcus could see the strange rune carved into the leather and filled in with some kind of metallic paint.

Maelen unbuckled the leather coat and inside Marcus could make out what looked like an entire book printed in those same symbols and filled in using the same kind of silver paint.

“On my palm is a focus, it allows me to direct my will, kind of like a nozzle on a hose, you can narrow the spray to direct its power, same principal. But this, well this is more interesting” he continued pointing to the inside of the coat.

“Somewhere along the line someone created or found this particular runic script that we still use today. This spell for lack of a better word, describes the intent or action we want to perform, by simply focusing on it for a moment and releasing energy into it, it activates the spell, this one for instance is an armor spell” he finished.

Marcus stared at him for a moment trying to wrap his mind around what the old man was saying spells. Intent? What the hell had happened while he was away, he wondered.

Maelen’s expression fell as his eyes became distant, looking not really at anything but as if he were recalling a distant unpleasant memory.

“You see despite our evolution, despite our ingenuity at saving our species we are fundamentally animals at our core. We had discovered that we had been altered and given an amazing gift, our people spent years perfecting and understanding it, and then they began killing each other with it, once they discovered its potential, it wasn’t long before the tribes began perfecting Mage assassins, there job was simply to kill.

You see we had gone back to a time of simple weapons, swords, staffs and bows but with the discovery of the mage every group scrambled to push the envelope on what they could do simply to ensure they could overpower their rivals” he continued.

He leveled a sorrowful gaze at Marcus driving home his story as he continued “according to the records it was a slaughter, a lot of the academics who had returned.

The people with the real knowledge that could later help as they started to try and rebuild, were killed quickly, each tribe wanting to keep the knowledge for themselves while limiting what others could invent or rediscover. Like other times in history, a warlord appeared, banding together the tribes and ruling them as a single nation, later he was deified, we know him today as Aurtus” He said.

Marcus just leaned back breaking eye contact with Maelen and instead looking into the fire.

Anger grew in his stomach, so few people and yet still they fought and killed each other, setting us back as a civilization for who knew how many generations he thought bitterly.

Looking back at Maelen he could see the man understood and probably shared the sentiment. But the anger was impudent at best, there was nothing he could do about it; it was long done, and those people were long dead he realized.

Maelen nodded when he saw the anger diminish and continued “Now we are not sure how many generations later we had gone from about twenty thousand to over two hundred, but something interesting happened not every child born had the gift we are not sure how many but it is thought that maybe one in five or one in eight have some form of the gift, but only one in every thousand have the even half the power of the gift that was given us.” He said and Marcus stopped him.

“Why do you keep calling it the gift, people killed with it, I killed with it. It is not a gift Maelen, its more of a curse” he spat at him, he definitely didn’t think of it as a gift and for some reason Maelen’s use of the word bothered him.

“It is not good nor evil, its about how you choose to use it, let me finish, be patient” he said making a calming motion with his hand. “Now as more people were born and our society grew, we began to create small villages and then larger ones. We think it was about ten generations ago when the first true kingdoms were formed, and it was also about that time that Wic began to take hold as a global religion.

No one is sure who wrote the first tenets, or expounded on the story of that first warlord, but it was about this time that the book of Aurtus came to be.

The first recordings we have are wandering messengers entering villages, preaching and setting up small shacks to hold assembly, but it took hold and soon it was the religion of all the kingdoms. Now there are still pockets of other religions hanging around, but most are fringe and considered Pagan” he recalled warming his hands over the fire and putting a few more of the cut logs he had stacked into the fire to build it back up.

Marcus couldn’t help smiling at the thought of religions like his own Catholicism, Judaism, Muslim all being considered fringe and pagan. “Oh, the irony” he whispered to himself, joining Maelen in warming his hands.

The sun had begun to set, and the air was growing steadily colder. “Now we get a little better idea from here on, about a hundred and fifty years ago a group of those who share our gift joined together creating a tribe I guess you would call it; they would attack villages and towns using their gifts, killing and stealing. The group was growing rich, they were unstoppable, for a time but the kingdoms banded together along with the soldiers of the church and beat back this threat, they did it with the help of a man named Zathris, he was a powerful mage who had gathered a force to beat back his rogue brethren and then armed the church with weapons and armor that could resist magic, hindsight being what it is, that had been a mistake. But the church was not done, once they had been aided by the mages, they turned on them.

The lord emissary who headed the church handed down the word that those with abilities were evil, cast out from the kingdom of the sky and Mephis had bestowed powers on them to wreak havoc on earth.” Maelen stated but Marcus could hear the hate in his tone, and he shared it.

They had marked his kind for death with a simple decree he thought. Shaking off the anger Maelen continued “The decree came down to hunt down this group and any others with abilities and kill them. The church created an order called the sword of the faithful. They recruited and trained whole legions of soldiers, using what Zathris had taught them to create specialized soldiers, Mage killers, these killers were human, they did not possess the same gifts, but what they had was knowledge. They were not only efficient killers and highly trained soldiers, but they were also trained specifically to kill us and equipped with armor and weapons to counter our abilities, and they were very, very good at it. We were not able to affect their weapons or manipulate their minds, however we could still affect items around them and the environment, but they trained to hit first, hit hard and not let us cast. Within the year the group had been hunted and killed”.

Marcus interrupted shaking his head. “wait, they knew those abilities came with the people who had landed, how the hell can they call them evil” he asked astounded at the ignorance. Maelen smiled ironically. “this is generations later, the stories handed down from parent to child had changed no longer was it people returning to earth but now the gods had populated the earth with humans sending them down in the tears of metal” he said the smile was still on his face but there was no humor in it. Then he thought about Veric and his time at the keep with his friend.

“The religion is tolerant and gentle how could this group have spawned from that” he asked confused and Maelen nodded understanding. “It is, in fact one of the most tolerant religions I have ever seen, but people were scared Marcus, there will always be those who will use fear and any religion has its zealots, those who feel we are too lenient and those who feel the only path to heaven is paved with the blood of an enemy” he said lowering his head.

Marcus did the same humanity might have been given a second chance, but humans, no matter how enlightened were still humans he thought bitterly.

“The order didn’t stop there, they continued to hunt those with abilities, healers, leaders and anyone else it didn’t matter their age or position and killed them stating they were vanquishing evil. Now what they didn’t know was that Zathris, had only been on the planet for five years, an ARC volunteer, like us she landed later than expected.

She had blended in but when she saw what the church was doing with the knowledge she had collected and shared, she began to grow her small group, hiding them from the order.

Joan Zathris ironically was a devout Muslim and Army Ranger. Those she saved began to fight back, Zathris trained them in the ways of soldiers, but the order was too many and with the support of the community Zathris knew they would be stomped out sooner or later.

The order had chased her entire group of thirty people into a cave system. Joan used her abilities to bring down the caverns around them but saving the group inside. The order proclaimed themselves victorious, that Aurtus himself had smite them.” Maelen said and then pointed to a silver dragon pendant on the leather armor he wore.

“That day the Order of the Dragon was created, Joan and the group created a keep in those very same caverns, the tenants we live by were written and the council was formed. Our people began crafting weapons using the same method the order had except enhancing the properties instead of nullifying them, five years later, the church ashamed of the decree, reversed it and in a historic meeting the kingdoms, the church and the order met, signing the Agreement between Mage and Mundane” he said.

“Unknown to the mundane’s Zathris created the watchers, a group dedicated to finding and protecting those like himself, those who fall to earth, the fallen, like me and like you. But he also knew that sooner or later the Mages would be called to defend themselves so Zathris began to train an elite group within the Order, battle mages, I am a watcher and one of the last Battle Mages left to the order, which is why I was sent to find and train you, I fear we will be needed long before you are ready my friend”

Maelen reached behind his back and pulled out a length of what looked like decorative pipe, it was about three feet in length with dragon claws on each end, both holding a clear round crystal.

Along the grip’s dragon scales had been etched into it Marcus took a closer look and inlaid between the decorative scales were more symbols there seemed to be a pattern to the placement but he couldn’t quite make it out.

“Weapons like this” he said and then put it back setting it into a leather harness at the base of his back “Have been innovated since the time of Zathris”.

Maelen looked down and took a breath “Despite the possible danger, we will be going to the order as there is a person who you need to meet and who needs to meet you, but we will not be among friends, there are those who if they knew what you were, would ensure you never left. Your power, your ability represents a danger to some and something to attain for others.

So we will need to keep moving son, this isn’t the world I landed in, at that time my Order would have been a haven, but you have to understand, Mages are rare, mages with real power are unheard of and there are those in the order who are desperate and will stop at nothing to dissect you physically and magically to attain what you have, When I arrived they never asked where I came from and thankfully I never told them, but the word is out on you, everyone has been combing the country looking for the one who landed” He finished.

Marcus looked at him with disbelief, he had just been told that he wasn’t safe, wouldn’t be safe and might never be. “Why the hell would I go there, if I have no chance of being safe and if they figure out what I am.

They will probably chain me up in the basement and take me apart, we should just run Maelen, get away from all of this” he started looking at this man as if he had grown three heads.

Maelen shook his head but Marcus could see the sorrow on his face. “I’m sorry it that way, I’m sorry you showed up right when things were going to shit, but this person I need you to meet, can help and may be your only chance at being safe, if there was any other way” he broke off his eyes serious and brooding finishing where his words ended.

Marcus didn’t know this man, Maelen could have left him where he was, could have just walked away, or could have chained him, but he hadn’t, at the very least he didn’t mean Marcus immediate harm and if he was honest with himself, he needed someone.

Marcus would go with him for now, but unsaid was he reserved the right to bail if he wanted to. Maelen nodded back with a weak smile on his face rising the old man turned and headed for the Woodline.

“Hey” Marcus called with alarm “Where are you going?” Maelen turned and smiled back at him “Food man, we have to eat” he said and then continued walking.

Marcus reflected on what he had learned, humanity as a whole had been set back centuries by whatever had happened.

With no true record of the events they would never know the exact nature of the catastrophe and the attack.

Learning that the church had slaughtered and might still be slaughtering people because they were merely different told him that zealotry wasn’t dead. Even though those that founded this new humanity might have been more enlightened then their forefathers.

We as people tend to fall back on the same primal instincts he reflected. A sound from the bushes interrupted his thoughts as Maelen appeared carrying two plump rabbits.

They didn’t talk much while the older man dressed and cooked the two rabbits, Marcus watching the simple process, continuing to digest all he had learned through the entire meal, Maelen seemed to understand and left the younger man in silence during the meal.

“I know your faith in humanity is a bit shaken, mine was when I had discovered everything that had happened. But remember for every evil there is always two goods, or at least that is what WIC teaches hoss, not that I am very religious being a lapse catholic and all” Maelen finished smiling at Marcus.

Sitting around the fire still swathed in bandages watching Maelen balance between keeping warm and burning himself in the roaring fire.

“So, what do we do now?” Marcus inquired as he stared at the flames dancing over the rocks that surrounded the small pit.

As he looked around at the trees, noticing the small blue and green dancing lights that lit across the canopy the light from the fire hit the crystal formations around them, then to his surprise some began to move, he watched and then a breath of relief followed his recognition of the small phosphorescent primates as they played within the forest, the effect was surreal and beautiful as the purple, yellow and blue lights jumped between the trees chasing and playing with each other, it was calming and he quickly found himself smiling at the antics of the creatures.

Maelen’s words pulled him from the simple enjoyment of the forest creatures.

“We take you to the order, you’re not safe you killed collector’s which means you will be hunted by the crown, they will send a warden to bring you back, and if it gets back to the church or the Empress, hell even the Order and they figure out how you killed them, then if my hunch is right, you will have worse things to worry about” he stated and Marcus watched a shiver crawl down the old man’s back.

“The world is changing Maelen, who the hell is pulling the strings?” He asked and Maelen nodded. “Too many disappearances have happened in the last few years, whatever is going on, they have hands in more than one organization, there have been sightings of soldiers wearing a logo that most don’t recognize, Empress’s guards abducting children, new creatures seen in villages, the council might be turning a blind eye to the oncoming storm, but I most definitely am not hoss” Maelen finished locking eyes with Marcus and he could see the fear and worry in the old man’s face, he was scared of recent events, and that more than anything worried Marcus.

After a moment Maelen continued his earlier conversation. “We will teach you how to use your abilities and from there you can decide if you want to stay or if you want to live a normal life, I won’t force you to get the mark, with everything that is going on, someone has torn the agreement into shreds, so let’s keep you under the radar” he finished glancing over at Marcus as he sat there looking at the fire “Agreement?” Maelen had mentioned that before, as if he should know what that was and the old mage nodded realizing his mistake and the other man’s ignorance and explained “After the Mage Wars, I told you all sides got together and signed an agreement, well that agreement gave the Order the ability to police our own, thus creating the first mage laws. However, it was also written that anyone displaying the powers of a mage would have to carry a brand identifying them as such”.

He sat by the fire, waiting, meditating on what he learned, however it was difficult, the ache of Orah’s loss still with him constantly, standing he pulled the Falcatis and began moving through the blocks and parries, if just to take his mind off the loss of his love.

Maelen emerged a short time later from further down the tree line, carrying two rabbit carcasses. Seeing the old man appear, Marcus stowed the weapon and began to add more wood in anticipation of dinner.

The old mage handed the rabbits to the younger man who began to dress them and Gently place them on a spit, they both listened appreciatively to the meat as it began to sizzle and spit.

“I know you’re wondering how it was that I managed to bring two rabbits out of the woods with no traps” he stated a sly smile stretching over his face as he turned to the younger man.

Marcus shrugged nonchalantly but point of fact he was very curious, but he figured the old man used some of those ninja skills mixed with his powers.

Maelen looked out over the woods for a moment “Animals are primal creatures, we have the ability to sense what they are thinking and to push our intent at them in the form of simple images, this isn’t something we can do with people and if the animal is agitated or feeling threatened, it doesn’t work” he said.

Marcus stopped what he was doing and looked suspiciously at the old man is he putting me on he thought and Maelen looked back over at him

“I’m serious, not full conversations, but almost like pictures that form from the emotions or intent of the animal, it’s very basic but with practice you can talk and sometimes get the them to do what you want” he finished “like the rabbits, I gave them peaceful pictures, giving them a sense of home while I snuck up on them and then broke their necks before they realized it was false” he finished matter of factly.

Marcus shook his head “that’s cold man, I mean like peta would crucify you cold, well if they still existed that is” he finished and Maelen laughed “your probably right hoss, but hey we need to eat and its better than trying to drop a tree trunk on the damn things, they are fast” he finished and Marcus got a mental image of Maelen trying to quietly hover a large piece of wood to drop on the rabbits and that caused him to laugh, a deep belly laugh and it felt good.

“after dinner, we will practice a bit with that, it takes a bit of knack but maybe we can teach you the basics” he finished turning the meat on the spit. They ate a short time later the meat tasting incredible after the small bit of jerky for lunch and the long fast paced walking of the afternoon.

Darkness was only an hour out as the sun traveled downward, obscured by the skeletal silhouettes of the winter forest they still had enough light to see and once the bones were cleaned and buried Maelen motioned for the younger man to follow him.

They walked quietly in the underbrush, occasionally Maelen stopping them as he paused looking out over the woods, tilting and turning his head, his eyes closed as if he were listening for a far-off sound.

A few minutes they began to move again through the skeletal trees, Maelen pausing again every so often, only to move off in a different direction. Marcus was getting the feeling that he was being poked fun at when to his surprise as they crouched behind a large Oak Maelen motioned for the younger man to look, as he peeked around the tree and to his surprise about ten feet away, he caught sight of a grey rabbit as it lazily hopped around eating from the forest floor.

“Well fuck me” he whispered watching the animal. Despite their presence the animal seemed unbothered continuing to hop a few short steps and eating as if it didn’t even notice their presence.

Marcus shot a glance at the older man and could see the look of fierce concentration on his face. Is he talking to the damn rabbit now? he wondered closing his own eyes Marcus reached out with his mind trying to see if he could sense the animal.

It took him a few moments, his mind quieting and his consciousness stretching far into the field, he felt the static presence of the crystals and at first, he didn’t feel anything else, then suddenly, it was there a sense like a pulse, then another following it, almost like he was feeling the animal’s little heartbeat. Maelen slowly opened his eyes turning to Marcus “very carefully push a small amount of your will at the creature, it is easier to give it instruction then to figure out what’s its thinking, so form a simple picture in your mind, like a carrot or head of lettuce and push lightly at the rabbit, not too hard or it will be like a bullhorn in its head” Maelen whispered gently.

Marcus nodded, finding the small heartbeat of the rabbit again, he formed a picture of a carrot in his head and pulled in power, slowly he pushed the image at the small creature infusing it with a small piece of his will. Opening his eyes, he watched in amazement as the little rabbit shot straight up, its eyes the size of dinner plates before it fell over, dead.

“Great, I said lightly, now you scared the poor thing to death” Maelen admonished,

Marcus shrugged “Sorry” he mumbled, and they set about trying to find another. It didn’t take long until the two of them crawled up over a knoll to find another small rabbit eating in a field, this one was black, lean and young looking.

“Now, only a little power, we don’t need to kill anymore damn rabbits” Maelen whispered but the younger man could hear the smile in his tone, Marcus did as instructed, reaching out and finding power, he brought in a small amount, then forming the picture of the carrot he ever so slowly breathed it out, infusing his will gently, with a small amount of power. Then before he could push the image, another picture popped into his mind and then another after that in rapid fire succession both were blurry, Abandoning his own picture he concentrated on the images coming into his own mind, focusing on them they cleared up and he was able to see and understand them, first a rabbit den, then leafy greens and then another rabbit.

“What the hell” he breathed trying to get a sense of what he was seeing. He described what he was seeing to Maelen who smiled. “He’s thinking about food, home and chicks” Maelen translated with a chuckle “good job, not many can see the intent of an animal, you have a natural gift for it, it took me years to be able to see the thoughts of animals” he finished.

Shaking his head Marcus closed his eyes, watching the repetitive pictures flashing through the small animal’s mind. There was a beat to it, almost rhythmic in nature as If the small rabbit was reciting a prayer or practicing a verse he had to memorize.

The experience was surreal as both men crouched, watching, the rabbit continued its daily search for food oblivious to the machinations of the two mages nearby.

Marcus began to experiment, matching the picture style, he visualized a grouping of leafy greens and then scanning the area, found a tree and sent the picture while thinking of the location.

Almost instantly the creatures little head shot up looking around, Marcus thought they had been spotted.

Then he relaxed, it wasn’t agitated it was excited he thought, watching with interest. The rabbit began moving towards the far tree, its pace picking up as it got closer. It went around the far side, both men losing site of it.

But Marcus was smiling he had given the small animal an order and it had obeyed. It wasn’t as simple as talking or instructing but with a little practice, he could, what, become Marcus lord of the rabbits?, he considered for a moment and then a smile spread across his face as a mental picture of himself in shiny armor and pointing forward as a flood of small white furry rabbits stormed a castle almost making him laugh, but he quickly stifled it

“Death awaits with big nasty sharp pointy teeth” he muttered to himself in a horrible Scottish accent.

Maelen shot him a curious look but the younger man waived him off, that was one insight he didn’t want to share. They moved back to the camp that was incredible he thought shaking his head still in shock at the ability.

“What causes them to listen, how come we can see their thoughts, it’s not like we can just do it with anyone, right?” Marcus asked turning his statement into a question.

Maelen shook his head “Not sure, I mean there have been theories because the creatures spend so much time around the crystals that the exposure over both time and generations have altered the creatures and our own ability to sense the crystals gives us the ability to interact with them as we do with the crystals, but again it’s only a theory, we don’t exactly have a bunch of scientific instruments to measure the brain waves of the creatures.

We have come across creatures who have been altered, we call them tuned usually it’s their eyes that give it away, they are always bright blue, they are the easiest to talk to and sometimes, they can talk to you” he finished.

The two settled in for the night, Marcus watching the flames as the empty spits from that night’s meal still hung smoldering over the flames and he thought about the small creature and the possibilities, what other creatures could they do that with he wondered.

The next morning, they ate a quick breakfast of leftover rabbit and packed up the meager camp,

Marcus spent the morning walking through the series of moves and techniques. The older mage had shown him, practicing far into the early afternoon before Maelen motioned for him to join him both finally setting out, the old man was pushing them faster, Marcus could see the worry on his face, he recalled him talking about the Wardens and their ability to track fugitives, he had almost seemed reverent in his description, he feared them Marcus realized, the revelation not sitting well with him as they moved as at brisk pace.

He didn’t know what or who the Wardens were, but they were formidable enough to scare the older man and that was enough for Marcus as he picked up his pace despite the stinging pain from his healing wounds.

The two trudged through the woods quietly but Marcus was far from complacent as he spent the time reaching out, finding the crystal formations, the static energy easy to identify.

He allowed his mind to play over the forest, reaching out and at times rewarded with fuzzy pictures as he came across the mind of animals, they were fleeting some too far and others too foreign for Marcus to connect with, it was always frustratingly fleeting as if they were just on the edge of his ability to monitor them.

He had no idea what that distance or limit was. That brought up another interesting point did the more he used this ability, the stronger and further it got he wondered.

Another question to ask the old man, as they navigated a particularly thick brush line, Marcus stopped cold as a feeling of fear and hopelessness descended upon him like an anvil. “What the hell” he breathed calming himself, it took him a moment to realize the feeling wasn’t his “Maelen” he called the other man turning and giving Marcus a confused but concerned look.

Oh, I must be a sight he thought realizing he had almost descended into a full-blown panic attack “What’s wrong” Maelen said, taking a step towards him his head on a swivel searching the local area for any threats.

“You didn’t feel that, panic, fear?” Marcus asked doubling over as another wave hit him. Maelen cocked his head, continuing to look around “Feel what?” he asked and before Marcus could answer a fresh wave of raw primal emotion slammed down on him almost forcing him to his knees.

With a few calming breaths he was able to keep his feelings and balance under control.

Then he realized that as he calmed himself, he could sense a direction for the feelings. Something or someone was in trouble he thought, turning in a circle and ignoring the worried look Maelen was giving him homed in on the emotions.

facing the direction he thought it was, he ignored his wounds and took off at a run with Maelen’s protests quickly fading behind him, ignoring the slapping branches that scraped his skin and grabbed at his clothing Maelen’s worried shouts continued behind him but his mind was focused on the emotions Maelen’s warnings and shouts seeming a million miles away as he pushed faster into the brush.

Unlike earlier with the rabbit, these weren’t pictures but raw emotions as if something or someone was transmitting them, but not something human he realized, these were too primal, too basic.

Continuing to run through the underbrush, he could hear Maelen calling to him and the crashing of branches and leaves as the old mage ran to catch up. He probably thinks I have lost my mind he pondered darkly a small ironic smile spreading over his face and then quickly disappearing as another bout of fear slammed into him.

He heard it before he walked into the scene, snarling and small barks followed by yips of pain coming from somewhere in front of him.

Dogs he thought, they sounded like dogs and before he knew it, Marcus exploded into an open area and almost into two of the largest wolves he had ever seen, and that included his own little close call from a year ago.

“Fuck” he hissed coming up short and backpedaling as the two animals regarded him with hostile eyes their muzzles rising, and low vibration of growls emitted from two large lines of razor-sharp teeth on display for Marcus to appreciate.

He glanced around taking in the scene in front of him. Maelen coming in right behind him and almost slamming into his friend “Holy shit” he breathed behind Marcus “stay calm” he said in a panicked whisper as he too took in the scene.

Six of the large wolves surrounded a tree they stood there facing it and from the hackles and teeth they were hunting.

At the base of the tree was a younger much smaller wolf its bright blue eyes regarding the new arrivals, so bright they almost glowed Marcus thought as he locked eyes with the creature and again another bout of fear hit him this is the source he thought.

The wolf was much smaller than the others, Marcus noticed its leg was bleeding, trapped in a tangle of vines. He could guess the scene in front of him.

They had chased the smaller wolf and, in his desperation, to find a place to hide he had become tangled allowing the others to catch up. This was the poor creature’s last stand and Marcus recalled his own run in with wolves.

“Nope, you’re not killing today fuckers” he whispered and without thinking about it he walked over putting himself in front of the small pitiful creature its legs and body tangled in the vines hanging around the trunk of the tree.

“What the hell are you doing” Maelen called and Marcus had to smile. Maelen had the tone you would give to someone who had lost his mind.

“I got this” Marcus said locking eyes with his friend, hopefully convincing him he wasn’t stark raving mad.

From the look on Maelen’s face he wasn’t even close to convinced as he pulled out the Falcatis and faced the larger creatures, Marcus followed suit, with a whispered word the Falcatis extended into a full staff and power coursed through the runes along the shaft.

Marcus felt his friend pull in power and he followed suit as they stood their ground facing the pack of wolves, Maelen turned to face the younger man nodding his head, despite what he thought, Maelen had Marcus’s back and that made him smile.

Marcus nodded back and then turned to regard the smaller wolf, the beast looking up with its glowing blue eyes, those pitiful eyes, he felt a wave of hope washed over him.

He felt the torrent of primal emotion coming from the small wolf, it took all his concentration to not allow it to overtake his own. Maelen had not warned him about animals doing that he thought now was not the time to explore it. Turning back to the pack, he followed them with his eyes turning to ensure he faced the animals as they circled, the pack positioning themselves for an attack, the alpha lowering himself to the ground and stalking in a half circle, Marcus could see his hackles extended and his teeth bared, swallowing his own fear as well as that of the small wolf he stood his ground.

Marcus tensed trying to keep all of them in front of him, should one make it to his left or right, he would be dead, maybe this was a bad plan he admitted to himself, but he was committed now and there was no turning back. “Get out of here” he bellowed at the top of his lungs the two closest wolves cringing and jumping a little but none of them took off, they were not going to let their prey go that easily.

He could see them looking from him to the little wolf behind him, judging and calculating.

They are wondering if they can get to him before I can come to his defense he realized.

Why do they hate this one so much Marcus wondered shooting a quick glance at the smaller creature? The feeling of hope and fear hit him again the little wolf transmitting his feelings to Marcus seeing the human as his protector, he shook his head, he couldn’t let the emotions overwhelm him.

These beasts seem to revile the younger one, was it because it was different, did they sense his difference Marcus continued, pushing with his will and power he released a picture of death and danger, the large wolves flinched but otherwise stood their ground, Marcus could have kicked himself what had Maelen said, it didn’t work when they were agitated, angry or scared, this limits my options he thought looking over the tensing wolves as they prepared to attack.

He watched them with a detached interest, controlling his fear as the alpha as the alpha got the attention of his pack mates and without warning leapt at the human.

Quickly drawing in power Marcus didn’t bother with the focus instead releasing it like a shotgun blast at chest level. The alpha was brought up short and flung backwards as if hit by a giant invisible bat.

Crashing into the brush, the others looked on, ears flattening as they quickly backed off, he could hear the crashing as the alpha hit forest floor.

Marcus smiled but only for a moment as the Alpha running out of the woods and straight at Marcus.

“Oh shit” he said trying desperately to pull in power, but the blast had left him weak, he was too slow as the large beast launched himself, he was a dead man.

But before they could reach him a blast of fire exploded at the ground in front of him bringing the the animal up short and then Maelen, moving with speed he didn’t think the older mage possessed spun the quarterstaff, bringing it down into the side of one of the wolves and before it could utter a single protest, the staff was up and rammed into the side of the second, the old mage jumped back ten feet much to Marcus’s amazement and before he had landed, another blast of fire from his hands sent them running back into the woods, Marcus could hear the crashing as they continued to run further and further into the brush.

He turned to see Maelen holding the staff, the end pulsing red. The older man relaxing, and the staff’s glow diminished as it collapsed back to the smaller size, he put it away and walked over to the small wolf, much to Marcus’s amazement the man didn’t even look winded.

“That was incredible” Marcus said. “You okay” he asked, the older mage smiled weakly “I’m fine” he answered moving to take a seat on the ground near one of the large trees, turning to regard the young wolf he appraised the young animal as it shrank away, moving as far as its tangled body could Maelen did not make a move towards him, as if knowing it was scared and instead, inspected the animal’s wounds from afar and wincing as he saw the large cuts long its flank

Then he turned a curious look at Marcus “How did you know?” he asked searching the younger man’s face.

“It called out to me, I felt fear and anger, as if it had broadcast it out and then I figured out where it was strongest and followed it here” he finished and looked up at his friend.

Maelen looked troubled but didn’t say anything for a moment “I have never heard of an animal reaching out to us before, not without our first reaching out to it” he said.

Marcus shrugged “it’s possible I touched his consciousness when I was scanning the forest, I’m not sure” he finished and Maelen just nodded seeming to take this as a good an answer as any.

Turning the old mage touched a rune on his sleeve, with a whispered word Marcus watched as power gathered in front of the old mage and formed into a glowing red outline of an owl, the animal flew into the sky as Maelen stood there, the color in his eye fading to white, it did not shock Marcus as much as it did the last time he had performed this little trick. “When do I get to learn that little trick?” Marcus asked looking after the spectral animal, his eyes continuing to track the avian apparition, Maelen smiled “There are many tools we have at our disposal, the senpai, as it’s called will ensure we aren’t snuck up on by the wolves and like all things, it will come in time” he simply said.

Marcus got to his knees and slowly approached the fearful wolf who was still trapped but no longer struggling as the animal regarded him, silently looking the two over and whining.

“Hey buddy, I am going to try and help you, so don’t bite me okay” he said and the animal wagged his tale once, but still looked on in suspicion, as he reached his hand slowly towards it, the wolf just stood there silently. Marcus’s hand made contact with him, and he felt the animal flinch, but other than that he stayed still, another whine emitting from him as Marcus scratched at the matted and dirty coat as he reached carefully around under it and began to pull at the vines, untangling the creature while trying to keep the vines out of the wounds, this was not an easy task and took far longer because of that then it should have.

The wolf nuzzled his free hand and licked at it as Marcus praised the young wolf “what a good brave boy you are standing up to those mean wolves” he cooed and caught Maelen rolling his eyes at him, the wolf wagged his tail and gave Marcus a look that said “why yes I am” and continued to lick his hand.

Finally, he got the creature untangled and as soon as it was free, the young wolf bolted, heading towards the underbrush. But before it disappeared it turned and studied Marcus, giving him a quiet woof and a wag of its tail as if to say thank you and then it was gone.

The rustling branches the only evidence it had been there at all.

They both stood there silently for a moment listening to the creature as it pushed further away from them, The old man turning towards Marcus “I have never heard of an animal communicating with us and the fact that I didn’t hear it, makes this even odder” he finished turning and heading back into the brush.

“As for why the other wolves attacked it, I have seen that before, sometimes animals can sense that their kin are different, they don’t react well to it. Seeing the member as a danger” he finished.

Marcus didn’t like the explanation, but he accepted it. “When we reach the keep, the archivist will assist in training you, helping you to broaden your knowledge, you have incredible power Marcus, but you don’t know shit about using it” Maelen said smiling.

Marcus nodded, distracted as the spectral owl returned, landing on a branch above them and disappearing, Maelen’s eyes returning to him how the hell had he seen Marcus thought, filing it away yet another thing to discover, the two continued their trek, occasionally he could hear rustling of the brush off to his left.

Reaching out with his mind he could feel the little wolf, apparently still following them and he smiled as he thought about loyalty and friendship and with a slight push of will sent that out towards the noise in the forest.

Something told him that wasn’t the last they would see of the little wolf.

He felt better knowing he was out there, knowing the wolf identified with Marcus, ultimately he didn’t have many friends and welcomed the creature, reaching out with his mind he sent him a picture of a pack, the animal sent the primal equivalent of approval and he smiled as he continued to walk.
